An attacker could inject CRLF (`\r\n`) sequences to append arbitrary headers (like `Bcc:` or `Cc:`) or manipulate the email body.

 **Vulnerability:** Setting `redirect: 'error'` in `fetch` to prevent SSRF bypasses via HTTP redirects broke core functionality for endpoints that legitimately need to follow redirects (e.g., website scrapers encountering `http` to `https` redirects).
 **Learning:** You cannot simply disable redirects for features that depend on them. You must manually follow the redirect chain.
 **Prevention:** Implement a manual redirect loop (`redirect: 'manual'`) that intercepts `3xx` responses, extracts the `Location` header, validates the new URL against the SSRF rules (`isSafeUrl`), and only proceeds with the next `fetch` if safe.

+**Vulnerability:** The `isSafeUrl` function failed to properly extract and validate the embedded IPv4 address within an IPv4-mapped IPv6 address (e.g., `::ffff:127.0.0.1` or `::ffff:7f00:1`). +**Learning:** `net.isIPv6` returns true for IPv4-mapped addresses, but `net.isIPv4` returns false. Any custom SSRF check that validates IPv4 blocks must also parse and apply the same rules to the underlying IPv4 address inside mapped IPv6 formats.

+**Learning:** In canvas visualizers and animation loops, it is common to skip drawing when paused (e.g., when offscreen). fix: correct IPv4-mapped IPv6 parsing in SSRF validation

The `isSafeUrl` function failed to correctly extract the embedded IPv4
address from IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses that did not use zero-compression
(e.g., 0:0:0:0:0:ffff:127.0.0.1). This could bypass internal network
checks. This patch explicitly splits and expands zero-compressed segments
to accurately validate the prefix and extract the embedded IPv4 suffix.

This allowed attackers to bypass the blocklist and resolve a domain to an internal loopback interface, establishing an SSRF vulnerability.

Kassen lover ikke en levering på butikkens egen tillægsmetode

Afvises nummeret, sagde kassen »Dette bestilles for sig, med sin egen
levering«. På butikkens 0 kr.-metode til tillæg er det ikke sandt: ordren
går til butikken på den metode, og ingen sender den nogen steder. Kassen
siger nu kun, at den ikke lægges til ordren. På alle andre metoder er
beskeden som før.

oko_is_addon_shipping_method(), som både ordren og kassen spørger.

Kassen lover ikke en levering på butikkens egen tillægsmetode

levering«. På butikkens 0 kr.-metode til tillæg er det ikke sandt: ordren
går til butikken på den metode, og ingen sender den nogen steder. Kassen
siger nu kun, at den ikke lægges til ordren. På alle andre metoder er
beskeden som før.

oko_is_addon_shipping_method(), som både ordren og kassen spørger.

er bygget med msgfmt -c.

fix(transcript): the flat Copilot Chat format parses too

The pre-1.109 `.json` is a whole `ISerializableChatData` object with no log
entries — the initial state written as one document. Treating it as "one
kind: 0" is why there is no second parser for it, and it closes the gap the
PR description flagged: those files were being captured, stored, and
projected as a single malformed event.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(proto): two rustdoc links that pointed at private imports

`[`Message`]` and `[`ModelTier`]` resolved to the `use` statements
rather than the items, so `-D rustdoc::broken_intra_doc_links` — which CI
runs — failed the whole crate. Plain code spans: the names are unambiguous
in context, and a doc link that needs a path to work is a doc link that
will break again the next time the imports move.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(state): a rustdoc link to a method that no longer exists

`[`Self::tenant`]` pointed at `AppState::tenant`, which was replaced by
`Principal::tenant` when the principal was resolved once in middleware
(D10). CI runs `-D rustdoc::broken_intra_doc_links`, so this failed the
crate.

fix: use npm pack --ignore-scripts to work around pnpm symlinks

jsii-pacmak defaults to `npm pack <path>` which crashes (npm error: Exit
handler never called) when node_modules uses pnpm's symlinked virtual
store. Passing any non-default --pack-command causes jsii-pacmak to
copy the module with dereference:true first, then run the command in the
resolved copy where npm pack succeeds.

dorny/paths-filter doesn't support ~1 suffix in the base parameter —
git fetch treats it as an invalid refspec. Resolve the parent SHA
explicitly via git rev-parse before passing to paths-filter.

Co-authored-by: nhanuman <naveen.ah@google.com>
Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

files.patch_head:
@@ -74,10 +74,14 @@ jobs:
       - uses: actions/checkout@v4
         with:
           ref: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha }}
+          fetch-depth: 2
+      - name: Resolve base commit
+        id: base
+        run: echo "sha=$(git rev-parse HEAD~1)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
       - uses: dorny/paths-filter@v3
         id: filter
         with:
-          base: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha }}~1

will break again the next time the imports move.

files.patch_head:
@@ -0,0 +1,3 @@
+type: fix
+
+The classic EF6 `DbContextBuilder<T>` seeds the database only on the first `Build()`/`BuildAsync()` call: later builds on the same builder return another context over the already-seeded database instead of inserting the seed data again, and the `SeedWith*` methods throw `InvalidOperationException` after the first build (selecting the provider again with `UseEffort()` starts a new, empty database), matching the EF Core builder.
